regulatory_evidence.text: 46.4 The policy must include  clear process es and indicate reasons, manner, timing etc. pertaining to  invocation/release of pledge and  liquidation of unpaid securities. Such policy must indicate the maximum period (shall not exceed five trading days from the pay-out date) within which the client must meet the payment obligation.

46.8 If the client fails to meet the payment obligation within the prescribed timeline, the TM shall, in accordance with its policy, invoke the pledge and liquidate the unpaid securities . The TM shall give reasonable notice to the client before invocation of pledge and liquidation of unpaid securities.

46.5 While unpaid securities pledged to CUSPA of TM may be considered for reporting client margin collection to Clearing Corporation, the TM shall not allow exposure on the basis of such securities to the client.

policy_evidence.text: Clients must meet the funds obligation for unpaid securities within **seven trading days from the pay-out date**.

If the client has not paid by the end of the payment period, Operations may invoke the pledge and sell the unpaid securities on any subsequent trading day. The client is notified by email after the sale.
Unpaid securities held under pledge may be considered towards the client's margin requirement and towards the client's exposure in the cash segment until the pledge is released.

Unpaid securities received in pay-out are credited to the client's demat account. Operations then marks a pledge on the unpaid quantity in favour of the pledge account on the next working day after pay-out, once the day-end funds obligation report has been reconciled.

regulatory_source.title: Handling of Client’s Unpaid Securities by Trading Members

retrieval.query: SEBI has decided to permit creation of standing instructions for Systematic Withdrawal Plans (SWP) and Systematic Transfer Plans (STP) for mutual fund units held in demat form, to be implemented in two phases (unit-based then amount-based). Depositories are designated as nodal facilitators and are directed to implement the framework, publish a standard framework, amend rules/bye-laws as necessary, make system changes, and disseminate the circular on their websites within specified timelines. Act as the nodal facilitator for implementation of the SWP/STP-in-demat framework. Ensure implementation of Phase - I (unit-based SWP/STP) by January 31, 2027. Ensure implementation of Phase - II (amount-based SWP/STP) by April 30, 2027. Make available in Phase - I the facility for "Unit-based SWP / STP" (standing instructions based on fixed number of units to be redeemed or transferred to another scheme). Make available in Phase - II the facility for "Amount-based SWP / STP" (standing instructions for fixed amount pay-out or for purchasing units of another scheme). Jointly publish a standard framework on Depositories' websites to operationalize the facility.

regulatory_evidence.text: Depositories shall be the nodal facilitator for implementation of this framework and shall  ensure the implementation of Phase - I by January 31, 2027  and implementation of Phase - ll by April 30, 2027.

In Phase - I, the facility shall be made available for “Unit-based SWP / STP” i.e. standing instructions based on fixed number of units to be
redeemed at a specified frequency for withdrawal or for purchasing units of another scheme of the same Mutual Fund.

In Phase - ll, the facility shall be extended to  “Amount-based SWP / STP” i.e. standing instruction for fixed amount which is required as
pay-out at a specified frequency or for purchasing units of another scheme of the same Mutual Fund.

retrieval.query: SEBI requires all regulated entities to report cyber incidents promptly: initial notification via mkt_incidents@sebi.gov.in within 6 hours and via SEBI's Incident Reporting Portal within 24 hours; reporting must be done through SEBI's portal (https://siportal.sebi.gov.in) which is aligned with the FSB's FIRE format, allow staged updates through the incident lifecycle (including continuing updates until final closure), and entities must put in place systems (including any necessary amendments to bye-laws, rules or regulations) to implement this circular. Notify SEBI via email (mkt_incidents@sebi.gov.in) of cyber incidents within 6 hours. Report cyber incidents on SEBI's Incident Reporting Portal within 24 hours. Report cyber incidents through the Cyber Incident Reporting Portal of SEBI (access via https://siportal.sebi.gov.in). Provide staged reporting (initial report, intermediate updates and final closure) and continue sharing updates until the incident is resolved. Use the FIRE format (Format for Incident Reporting Exchange) as implemented on SEBI's Incident Reporting Portal for incident submissions. Put in place systems and take necessary steps (including amendments to relevant bye-laws, rules and regulations, if any) to implement this circular.

regulatory_evidence.text: 2. SEBI has already prescribed guidelines for reporting of cyber incidents under Annexure-O (B: Guidelines on Handling Cybersecurity Incidents ) of CSCRF framework, mandating that all regulated entities report cyber incident through mkt_incidents@sebi.gov.in within 6 hours and SEBI Incident Reporting Portal within 24 hours.

3. In order to streamline the reporting of cyber incidents, SEBI has aligned its Incident Reporting Portal with “Format for Incident Reporting Exchange (FIRE)” Framework developed by Financial Stability Board (FSB). FIRE enables a structured incident reporting by defining common information fields, standardized definitions, and consistent classification of incident attributes promoting harmonisation across sectors or jurisdictions.

4. The portal will facilitate reporting of incidents in stages to reflect incident life cycle from initial reporting to intermediate updates and final closure, while acknowledging that certain information may not be available at the time of initial reporting.

policy_evidence.text:
POL-002 — Cyber Incident Response and Regulatory Reporting Policy §4.2 Staged reporting
The report on the SEBI portal is updated at each material development — containment, root cause, restoration — and a final
closure report is filed on the portal when the incident is resolved. The CISO owns each update; Compliance reviews it before
submission.

regulatory_source.title: Alignment of SEBI's Cyber Incident Reporting Portal with FIRE Format
